1. The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant/s - original claimant/s - legal heirs of the deceased - Hitendrasinh Banesingbhai Chauhan,
being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 06.02.2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Dhrangadhra in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.131 of 2003, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.4,80,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding Opponents No.1 to 3 i.e. driver, owner and insurance company of the Truck liable, jointly and severally.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1

That on 30.05.2003 at about 18:30 hours, deceased - Hitendrasinh Banesingbhai Chauhan was standing with his motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ-13-V-2458 on the public road leading from Bhuj to Madhapar.
At that time, on account of the rashness and negligence of opponent No.1 - driver of the Truck bearing registration No.GJ-12-V-5140 dashed and collided with the deceased.
As a result, the deceased received serious injuries and ultimately, he succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased - parents and widow have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1 and 2 - driver and owner of the Truck have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Opponent No.3 - Insurance Company of the Truck has appeared and has filed its written statement / objections by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the claimant/s for enhancement.
3. Learned advocate Mr. Henil M. Shah for the appellant/s - claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his monthly income was Rs.3,900/-, which the Tribunal has rightly considered.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has not considered the prospective income of the deceased while awarding compensation.
He has also submitted that the Tribunal has not properly applied multiplier, which should be 18 instead of 15.
He has fairly submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the deduction of personal expenses looking to the age of the deceased.

He has submitted that therefore, considering the loss of dependency, it would be calculated as Rs.3,900/- as monthly income plus 40% prospective income minus 1/3 as personal expenses multiplied by 12 months and multiplied by 18 multiplier would come to Rs.7,86,240/- total future loss, which should be awarded to the claimants by the learned Tribunal.

He has further submitted that considering the general and non-pecuniary damages, the learned Tribunal should award Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined funeral expenses.

He has also submitted that towards loss of consortium, there are three dependents and therefore, it would be awarded Rs.48,400/- to each dependent as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @

4. Per contra, Ms. Dave, learned advocate for respondent - Insurance Company has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.

She has submitted that there are no details of owner of the insurance of motorcycle and RC book of the vehicle as well as driving licence of the deceased submitted by the original claimants in support of their case.
She has further submitted that the policy of the truck is of the package policy.
She has also submitted that the motorcycle owner and insurance company were not joined as party in the claim petition.
She has further submitted that there is no income proof of the deceased.
Though salary certificate issued by Ram Fertilizer was produced.
Therefore, the income considered by the Tribunal is on higher side.

She has further NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/08/2024 undefined submitted that if minimum wage was considered at the relevant time, it should be Rs.2,300/- per month and not Rs.3,900/- per month.
She has submitted that the deceased was driving motorcycle and accident took place on head on collusion.
She has submitted that looking to the contents of the FIR and Panchnama, the deceased was himself negligent for the accident.
She has submitted that contributory negligence may be considered by both the vehicles.
She has submitted that under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation.
She has submitted that appropriate order may be passed.

sentences.text: It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined 6.1
I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

From the record, it transpires that the deceased was aged about 24 years and was serving as a Field Officer at Fertilizer Company and was also doing agriculture work and his monthly income was Rs.3,900/-
at the relevant point of time, which is supported by the salary certificate.
The Tribunal has considered the revenue records and salary certificate at Exh.30 as well as deposition of the applicants / claimants and their witnesses and decided the income of the deceased.
Therefore, it should be considered as monthly income of the deceased.

Hence, the monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.3,900/- per month and by adding 40% prospective income looking to the age of the deceased and dependents, as not calculated by the learned Tribunal, it would come to Rs.1,560/- and therefore, total income comes to Rs.5,460/- per month.
Since the deceased is aged about 24 years and there are three dependents, 1/3 would be proper to be deducted as personal expenses and therefore, it would come to Rs.1,820/-.

Hence, the income would come to Rs.3,640/-
per month and therefore, yearly, it would come to Rs.43,680/- and applying 18 multiplier as per the schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act as well as the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT

DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined the case of Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, it would come to Rs.7,86,240/- as future loss, which is required to be awarded to the claimants.

6.3 Further, there are three dependents to the deceased.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, Rs.40,000/- consortium to each dependent and 10%
rise, which comes to Rs.48,400/- as consortium to each dependent, which total comes to Rs.1,45,200/-, which should be awarded to the claimants.

The contentions raised by the insurance company are rejected.
6.5 Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.

Particulars Amount (Rs.)
 Future Loss of Income 7,86,240/-
 Loss of Estate 18,150/-
 Funeral Expenses 18,150/-
 Loss of consortium 1,45,200/-
 Total... 9,67,740/-
 Less : Amount which is already awarded 4,80,000/-
 Additional amount which is awarded 4,87,740/-
7.

Therefore, I hold that the claimant/s are entitled to get the total amount of compensation of Rs.9,67,740/- with NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined 9% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.

The Tribunal has already awarded Rs.4,80,000/-, therefore, remaining amount of Rs.4,87,740/- would be the enhanced amount of compensation payable to the claimant/s.
8.
For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.

8.2 The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount Rs.4,87,740/- with 9% p.a. interest from the date of claim petition till its realisation before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

8.3 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/325/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/08/2024 undefined deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
